name: physical activity prescription overview
title: Writing a physical activity prescription: first check it is safe (absolute contraindications stop it; otherwise stratify cardiovascular risk to decide how to start), then write the dose with F.I.T.T., then tailor it for hypertension and blood pressure medications; adjust if pain or swelling follows

root.title: Prescribe physical activity like a drug: is it SAFE, then what DOSE?
lines: ask: current activity · intentions · past activity + preferences · is it safe (symptoms, history)?
biggest gain: from NONE to SOME, so target sedentary patients

groups.title: 3 · TAILOR IT
lines: blood pressure is not a reason to skip exercise

head: h
Absolute contraindication
any ONE stops it
do: BP > 180/100: control with medication BEFORE exercise

head: h
Stratify cardiovascular risk
start low, go slow if sedentary
check: • chest, neck, jaw or arm pain
• breathless at rest or mild exertion
avoid: stop and promptly evaluate or refer: warn patients of these

head: h
F.I.T.T.
target ≥ 150 min a week, moderate-vigorous
do: • aerobic: walk, cycle, dance, swim, jog
avoid: • pain that does not settle after
• more night pain or joint swelling

head: h
Hypertension
check: if not, control it with medication first
do: • protect joints if obese or inactive
avoid: • vigorous exercise with left ventricular hypertrophy

head: h
Blood pressure medications
do: • angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor or angiotensin receptor blocker: minimal problems
• calcium channel blocker: extend the warm-down (postural hypotension)
avoid: ↓ maximum heart rate and performance: BAD for high intensity, avoid in athletes (ACE inhibitor first)
~but they limit the hypertensive response to exercise
